title: The price of privacy
excerpts: Every zero-knowledge proof requires computational resources to generate.
DUST is the unit that measures this computational cost in Midnight.
Like gas in other blockchains, DUST represents the energy needed to keep data private.

title: What is DUST
excerpts: DUST is a cryptographic resource metric that measures the computational cost of generating ZK proofs.
More complex proofs (more inputs, more constraints) consume more DUST.
DUST is the bridge between privacy and efficiency.

codeBlocks.title: DUST concept

title: Why privacy costs resources
excerpts: ZK proofs require complex mathematical operations: hash operations, elliptic curve arithmetic.
Hundreds or thousands of these operations are needed for each proof.
This work makes privacy possible but also costly.

title: The DUST balance
excerpts: Users must maintain a DUST balance to perform private operations.
This balance is separate from the token balance.
Understanding DUST is essential for building efficient private applications.

codeBlocks.title: DUST balance check

title: ZK proof generation resources
excerpts: Generating a ZK proof requires CPU for cryptographic operations.
Memory is needed for storing intermediate values.
Time is required for the proof to be computed.

title: Factors affecting DUST cost
excerpts: DUST cost depends on: number of witness variables.
Number of constraints in the circuit.
Proof system used.

codeBlocks.title: DUST formula

title: Proof complexity trade-offs
excerpts: There's always a trade-off between privacy and cost.
More private proofs require larger circuits and more DUST.
Understanding this helps design efficient systems.

title: Estimating DUST for your circuit
excerpts: Before deploying, analyze the circuit to estimate DUST costs.
Counting constraints and witness variables gives a good approximation.
This helps users plan their DUST budget.

codeBlocks.title: DUST estimation

title: The proof server role
excerpts: Proof generation is often delegated to specialized servers.
These servers perform heavy cryptographic computations off-chain.
This enables lightweight clients that consume DUST via the server.

title: How proof servers work
excerpts: User provides witness data (encrypted).
Proof server generates the ZK proof, consuming DUST.
The proof is returned to the user.

codeBlocks.title: Proof server flow

title: Trust model for proof servers
excerpts: Proof servers cannot see private data because it's provided as encrypted witnesses.
The integrity of the proof is guaranteed cryptographically.
No need to trust the server - the math ensures correctness.

codeBlocks.title: Encrypted witness

title: Decentralized proof generation
excerpts: Midnight supports a network of proof servers.
Users can choose their proof server or run their own.
Competition among providers helps keep costs reasonable.

title: Circuit optimization strategies
excerpts: Reduce the number of constraints in your circuits.
Reuse computation where possible.
Choose efficient hash functions. Smaller circuits consume less DUST.

codeBlocks.title: Optimized circuit

title: Proof aggregation
excerpts: Multiple actions can be proven together in a single proof.
This reduces the amortized DUST cost per action.
Batch operations are more efficient.

codeBlocks.title: Aggregated proof

title: Caching proofs
excerpts: For repeated operations, cache proofs.
Some data doesn't change between operations.
Reusing proofs avoids regenerating them and saves DUST.

codeBlocks.title: Proof cache

title: Balancing privacy and cost
excerpts: Privacy is a feature that costs DUST.
Design systems that give users control over the trade-off.
Allow users to choose their privacy level for each operation.
